content: Oseltamivir is a medication prescribed to treat certain types of influenza (commonly known as the flu) in adults and children over the age of one. It is most effective when taken within two days of the onset of flu symptoms. Additionally, it can be used to prevent certain types of flu in individuals who have been exposed to someone with the flu or during a flu outbreak. Oseltamivir belongs to a class of drugs called neuraminidase inhibitors, which work by inhibiting the spread of the influenza virus within the body. This medication helps reduce the duration of flu symptoms, such as nasal congestion, sore throat, cough, muscle or joint pain, fatigue, headache, fever, and chills. However, it does not prevent bacterial infections that may arise as complications of the flu. Oseltamivir is available in two forms: capsules and an oral suspension (liquid). When used to treat flu symptoms, it is typically taken twice daily (morning and evening) for five days. For flu prevention, it is usually taken once daily for at least ten days or up to six weeks during a community flu outbreak. It can be taken with or without food, but taking it with food or milk may reduce the likelihood of stomach upset. It is essential to follow the instructions on the prescription label carefully and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Do not take more or less of the medication or take it more frequently than prescribed. Open the bottle by pressing down on the cap while turning it. 3. Push the plunger of the provided measuring device completely down to the tip. 4. Insert the tip of the measuring device firmly into the bottle's opening. 5. Turn the bottle upside down and slowly pull back on the plunger until the prescribed amount of liquid fills the device to the appropriate marking. 6. Turn the bottle right side up and carefully remove the measuring device. 7. Administer the medication directly into your mouth from the measuring device without mixing it with other liquids. 8. Replace the cap on the bottle securely. 9. Disassemble the measuring device, rinse its parts under running tap water, and allow them to air dry before reassembling for the next use. Continue taking oseltamivir for the full duration of the prescription, even if you start feeling better. Stopping the medication too soon or skipping doses may result in incomplete treatment or inadequate flu prevention. If your symptoms worsen, new symptoms develop, or your flu symptoms do not improve, contact your doctor. Oseltamivir may also be used to treat and prevent infections caused by avian influenza (bird flu), a virus that primarily infects birds but can cause severe illness in humans. Before taking oseltamivir, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to oseltamivir or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are currently taking or plan to take. Certain medications, such as those affecting the immune system (e.g., azathioprine, cyclosporine, methotrexate, sirolimus, tacrolimus, or oral steroids like prednisone), may require dose adjustments or careful monitoring for side effects. Inform your doctor if you have previously taken oseltamivir to treat or prevent the flu, or if you have any conditions affecting your immune system (e.g., HIV/AIDS) or other medical conditions such as heart, liver, lung, or kidney disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, discuss this with your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking oseltamivir, notify your doctor immediately. Be aware that some individuals, particularly children, have experienced confusion, abnormal behavior, or self-harm while taking oseltamivir. If you or your child exhibit any of these symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. Oseltamivir does not replace the need for an annual flu vaccine. If you have received or plan to receive the intranasal flu vaccine (FluMist), inform your doctor, as oseltamivir may interfere with the vaccine's effectiveness if taken within two weeks after or 48 hours before the vaccine is administered. If you miss a dose of oseltamivir, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is within two hours of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. If you miss multiple doses, contact your doctor for further instructions. Oseltamivir may cause mild side effects, including nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, diarrhea, headache, difficulty sleeping, cough, or dizziness. If these symptoms persist or worsen, inform your doctor. Severe side effects, such as skin rash, hives, blisters, itching, swelling of the face or tongue, difficulty breathing or swallowing, or hoarseness, require immediate medical attention. Store oseltamivir capsules at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture. Keep the liquid form refrigerated but do not freeze it. Discard any unused liquid medication after ten days. Properly dispose of expired or unneeded medication by consulting your pharmacist. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222 or call emergency services at 911 if the individual has collapsed or is not breathing. Symptoms of overdose may include nausea and vomiting. Oseltamivir does not prevent the transmission of the flu to others. Practice good hygiene, such as frequent handwashing and avoiding the sharing of cups or utensils, to reduce the spread of the virus. Do not share your medication with others, and note that your prescription is likely not refillable. If flu symptoms persist after completing the medication, consult your doctor. Oseltamivir is marketed under the brand name Tamiflu®.
